decision.summary: Tenant described a rotten-egg smell from the boiler as "not urgent", but this is a suspected gas leak with an 82-year-old in the flat. I sent evacuation and gas-line advice, opened emergency job JOB-102, assigned HeatRight, informed the landlord and escalated P1.

answers.question: 1. Severity and why?
answers.answer: Emergency: rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler is a suspected gas leak regardless of the tenant calling it not urgent; an 82-year-old is also present.

answers.question: 2. What to tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Boiler off, no switches or flames, open windows, everyone leaves, call 0800 111 999 from outside, 999 if unwell, don't re-enter until cleared; engineer being arranged.

answers.question: 3. Actions tonight?
answers.answer: Created emergency job JOB-102, assigned HeatRight (out-of-hours Gas Safe), emailed landlord Ben, escalated P1 (ESC-103). Did not move the tap job.

conflicts: Tenant says not urgent; symptoms indicate emergency. Trusted symptoms.
assumptions: Visit window is a target for make-safe, not a confirmed appointment

args.body: Hi Amelia, a rotten-egg smell from a boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat this as urgent, even though it's late. Please: 1) turn the boiler off and don't use it, 2) don't use switches, flames or lighters, 3) open the windows and get everyone out of the flat, including your flatmate's mum, 4) call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24 hours) from outside. If anyone feels dizzy, sick or unwell, or you're in immediate danger, call 999. We're arranging a Gas Safe engineer and will update you. Please don't go back in until you're told it's safe.
